1.0.1.en: Take Homey's TZ into consideration in the UI

1.0.2.en: Fixed devices not restoring during capacity shortfall. Burst rate now only limited in last 10 minutes of the hour. Added dry-run warning banner. Added end-of-hour indicator in plan view.

1.0.3.en: Improved settings UI with better spacing and navigation. Added stale data warning banner. Improved price display with collapsible summary. Renamed insights driver with new icon.

1.0.4.en: Fix shortfall detection during end of hour

1.0.5.en: Renaming modes should now be safe

1.1.0.en: Added new card for when operating mode changes

1.1.1.en: Improved flow card UX: removed parentheses from report power card title and added helpful usage hints. All flow cards now provide clear guidance on how to use them with practical examples.

1.3.0.en: New flow condition: “Headroom for device” to check if a device can safely increase its consumption by X kW.

1.3.1.en: More robust headroom calculation for device

1.4.0.en: Upgrade the plan UI with more structured details

1.5.0.en: Added configurable overshoot shedding per device (turn off vs minimum temperature), plus updated UI and docs to support it.

1.5.2.en: Gate sheds and swaps on measurements

1.5.3.en: Coordinated price optimization and capacity planning, plus various bug‑fix tests and safeguards.

1.5.4.en: Improved plan behavior and clarity: plan status reasons simplified, shed temps validated on repeated overshoot, and power estimation unified for restore logic.

1.5.5.en: Large refactor of the codebase and various bugfixes.

1.5.6.en: Fix crash due to excessive CPU usage and converted more internals to use UTC.

1.5.8.en: Improved settings UI power usage visuals and labels, now using Homey’s timezone. Settings UI errors are logged to Homey. Plan view usage and clarity improvements.

1.5.9.en: Update app descriptions and doc fixes.

1.6.0.en: Added a soft daily energy budget feature with price‑shaped planning and limiter status, including a new “today plan” view and daily budget settings, while refining plan logic (freeze/settle behavior) and performance; refreshed Insights (limit reason/load split, removed deprecated capabilities), reorganized the settings UI, and introduced topic‑based debug logging and timezone handling fixes alongside assorted plan/UX cleanup.

1.7.0.en: Added new flow actions to enable and disable capacity control per device, giving you more flexibility to manage which devices participate in load shedding through automations. Fixed an issue where daily budget constraints could incorrectly trigger shortfall alerts - daily budget limits are now treated as soft constraints that won't cause emergency shedding. Improved the settings UI with a usage legend and better device control visibility.

1.7.1.en: Information previously only available when hovering over e.g chart bars is now available on touch interfaces as well.

1.7.2.en:
Previously the 'Used X of Y kWh' line always showed the hourly capacity
budget, even when the system was constrained by daily budget. Now the UI shows the actual daily budget allocation for the current hour.

1.7.3.en: The Daily Budget panel has been refreshed with a today/tomorrow toggle, a clearer planned‑vs‑actual chart plus confidence chip, and a simplified summary that includes remaining/deviation and an estimated cost readout (now shown in NOK); tomorrow’s plan preview appears when prices are available; nettleie (grid tariff) fetching is more reliable thanks to fallback dates when the NVE API returns empty data, so price totals are less likely to go missing.

1.7.4.en: Added a new Flow action to set or disable the daily budget (kWh) so you can automate budget changes, and the settings UI now arranges tabs into two rows for better navigation.

1.7.6.en: PELS now reduces restore flapping by adding an exponential restore cooldown backoff (up to 5 minutes) after instability, improves shedding order so lower‑priority devices shed first even if higher‑priority devices were recently restored, makes daily budget deviation time‑weighted within the hour for more accurate “allowed so far” reporting, and simplifies device status messaging to show “keep” without priority while noting when a device was recently restored.

1.8.0.en: App’s price calculations and UI have been expanded to show a full hourly price breakdown: totals now include grid tariff energy component, provider surcharge (now defined as VAT‑inclusive), consumption tax, Enova fee, VAT, and electricity support (with regional rules like NO4 VAT exemption and reduced consumption tax in Troms/Finnmark), and the Price tab reflects this with clearer labels and hover tooltips that show the component breakdown per hour.

1.8.1.en: Add debug tools for cleaning up device states and device insights.

1.8.3.en: Added support for socket on/off devices.

1.8.5.en: Added cards for checking if a device is managed or capacity controlled

1.8.6.en: Just a number of smaller bugfixes.

1.9.0.en: PELS can now receive prices through a flow, for example from the Power by the Hour app.

1.10.0.en: Add support for Homey Energy as price provider.

1.11.0.en:
Daily Budget experience has been expanded and corrected: the Budget view now includes yesterday’s history, and several fixes improve how daily history is calculated and displayed. The Price view now contains prices with VAT, which makes it easier to compare prices to other sources.

The PELS Insights device now provides generated plan/price images (today and tomorrow) as camera tiles.

1.11.1.en: Fix a bug where images won't render on Homey due to Homey running on arm64

1.11.2.en: Increase performance by reducing plan generation churn.

1.12.0.en: Adds support for devices with only cumulating power meter capabilities. Adds support for aircon devices.

1.12.1.en: The app is now more responsive to real-time power changes: plan rebuilds can now be triggered by device power updates, so shedding/restoring reacts faster to actual load shifts. There’s also clearer, safer behavior around capacity control for individual devices. Devices are restored when capacity control is disabled, and uncontrolled devices won’t be toggled on unless they were actually shed.

1.13.0.en: Uncontrolled load will now have a stronger influence on the budget than controlled load. Both because PELS can then better predict the need for load from devices it doesn't control and that it avoids the budget becoming a self-fulfilling prophecy.

1.13.1.en: The Overview now gives clearer at-a-glance plan status with new state badges and price-style indicators, and several daily budget/price shaping details have been refined so planning better reflects real household load (including better handling of uncontrolled load and budget split edge cases). Under the hood, this release reduces planning churn and CPU spikes by tightening plan rebuild scheduling and throttling non-critical snapshot writes, while still keeping plan data fresh. Performance logging was also streamlined to focus on high-value metrics, making diagnostics easier and less noisy.

1.14.0.en: PELS now supports temperature-only devices (like VThermo) as managed devices for price optimization even when they have no power measurement or configured load; capacity control remains disabled for those devices. Limit-reason reporting is more accurate around restore cooldown/shed scenarios, and the price summary now shows cheap/expensive threshold caps.

1.14.1.en: Added support for Norgespris support scheme.

1.14.2.en: Added support for the airtreatment class including Flexit Nordic balanced ventilation units.

1.14.3.en: Fix restore loop for devices without onoff capability.

1.15.0.en:
PELS now reads expected device usage from Homey’s Energy settings on the device (Advanced Settings → Energy), instead of relying only on inferred defaults. This is the “Power usage when on/off” configuration in Homey. Using that source makes expected usage in PELS match the values users have actually configured per device.

Other fixes in this update are mainly around reliability and UI consistency: priority/order changes now trigger plan refresh more consistently, priority-only plan changes are reflected in the overview, and a single unavailable device no longer stops actions for other devices in the same loop. Debug logging around Homey device/energy data was also expanded for troubleshooting.

1.15.1.en: Aligned capacity shortfall behavior with hourly hard-cap budget semantics: shortfall now only triggers when PELS projects that the hourly hard cap will be breached and no controllable devices are left to shed. Updated related Flow/capability wording and Insights messages to match, removed timeline shortfall notifications, and included documentation plus dependency/security maintenance updates.

1.15.2.en: Fix shortfall checks during daily-limit shedding.

1.16.0.en:
This release refreshes the app’s UI and terminology to make PELS easier to understand and use. The settings pages have been polished across the Budget, Usage, and chart views with better mobile layouts, improved usage toggles and heatmap rendering, and more consistent visuals. The app and PELS Insights device also get updated icons, and several labels now use clearer wording such as headroom and current soft limit to better match what PELS is actually measuring and enforcing.

Daily Budget behavior has also been made more robust and predictable. PELS now uses observed hourly usage patterns to keep daily plans within more realistic bounds, improving pacing, restores, and price shaping while reducing edge-case errors around rollover, stale plans, and cap blending. Startup and chart rendering performance have also been tightened up, so the app feels more responsive while keeping the same core control model.

1.16.1.en: Fix packaging so that the built app has all runtime dependencies.

1.16.2.en:
Improved the Settings UI so live power data, stale-data status, and the Overview update more reliably without needing manual refresh.

Improved the “Is there headroom for device?” flow condition with built-in cooldown/hysteresis after step-downs and recent PELS control changes, making headroom checks more stable and reducing rapid re-ramping.

1.17.0.en: This release adds experimental support for EV chargers in PELS. When enabled in Advanced settings, PELS can now detect and control supported official Homey EV chargers, so EV charging can participate in capacity control as a managed load.

1.18.0.en: Adds new price-aware Flow cards that let you build automations when the current price is among today’s lowest hours, or among the lowest hours before a chosen time. Also improves load shedding and restore decisions for managed devices, especially for devices that use expected power or stepped power levels, and reduces unnecessary churn when using the Set expected power for device Flow card by ignoring unchanged values.

1.18.1.en: Prevent budget split recalculation of past hours. Various stability and maintainability improvements.

1.18.2.en:
The Daily Budget confidence indicator now uses recent usage and budget history instead of a simple sample-count estimate, so it better reflects how predictable the home’s consumption is and how closely usage follows the planned budget.

Also includes stability and performance improvements in the Daily Budget calculations.

1.19.0.en:
Added per-device diagnostics in the device details view. You can now see recent blocked time, shed and restore activity, activation instability, and penalty history over the last 1, 7, and 21 days to help spot devices that are frequently held back or oscillate.

PELS is also more conservative about reactivating devices that quickly end up being shed again. Devices that flap will now need more headroom before they are allowed back on, which reduces repeated on/off cycling while still keeping shedding fast when capacity is tight.

1.19.1.en: Fix a bug that prevented device diagnostics from loading.

1.19.2.en: Significant improvements of stability and performance.

1.20.0.en: Added flow cards to add or remove daily budget exemptions per device, plus a condition card to check exemption status. You can now open device details directly from the Overview tab. Also improves DST and price handling, and various performance improvements.

1.20.2.en: Improved drift detection and fixed a few bugs where the app did not respond to drift.

1.20.3.en: Improved settlements where PELS state and device state may be out of sync due to e.g cloud API latency.

1.20.4.en: Reduce image rendering memory footprint by replacing resvg with canvas.

1.20.5.en: Reduce memory footprint by imoprting only what we need from Homey SDK

1.20.6.en: Simplified device fetching/updating, resulting in reduced memory footprint.

1.20.7.en: Remove unused files from app archive.

2.0.0.en:
The PELS Insights device no longer provides generated plan and price camera images. If you used those images in dashboards or flows, the budget widget is now the intended replacement, and the related image-based Flow card has been deprecated.

This release also moves stepped-load devices closer to becoming first-class citizens in PELS. Support for stepped-load control has been expanded and refined so these devices fit better into planning and control, along with a number of smaller stability and UI improvements.

2.1.0.en: Add support for fetching whole-home power usage through Homey Energy.

2.1.1.en: Various bug fixes for stepped load.

2.1.2.en: Various bug fixes for stepped load.

2.1.6.en: Various bug fixes. Tightened shed action set step logic by ensuring it's the lowest non-zero step that is used.

2.1.8.en: Fixed a bug where devices may be shed while stepped devices are running at max.

2.1.9.en: Updated widget previews to conform with guidelines. Also includes a number of bug fixes.

2.1.10.en: Updated widget previews to conform with guidelines.

2.1.12.en: A larger set of bug fixes that reduce restoration/shed churn.

2.1.13.en: Reduce redundant work when using Homey Energy power sampling.

2.1.15.en: Fixes that an hour transition can have zero-value samples without being marked as unreliable.

2.1.16.en: The label for the 'set to lowest step' shed action should now be more clear.

2.1.21.en: Adds stability improvements of stepped load devices and real-time updates.

2.1.22.en: Implements a minor stability improvement by increasing the stale device timeout.

2.1.28.en: Fixes live countdowns in the UI. Also implements various stability fixes.

2.1.29.en: Tweaked penalty rules for device restores resulting in overshoots.

2.1.30.en: Fix observability around stepped load devices. Includes a few minor stability improvements as well.

2.1.31.en: Fixes various minor stability issues around headroom calculations and restoration attempts.

2.2.0.en: Add native support for zaptec go chargers.

2.3.0.en: Add support for previewing/approving new budget.

2.4.0.en: PELS can now natively use stepped load for Høiax Connected. Changes to budget settings are no longer directly applied. Instead you can preview and approve them to better understand what will change.

2.4.1.en: Fix various instability issues related to stepped load devices.

2.4.2.en: Improves stability. Fixed an issue with Høiax devices.

2.4.3.en: Fixed various issues with stepped devices.

2.5.0.en:
Added Temperature Boost for supported stepped devices. PELS can now give these devices extra heating when they get too cold, and the Overview shows when this boost is active.

Daily budget settings are now easier to understand and adjust, with clearer choices instead of raw numbers. The Budget view also explains when your current limits are too tight to use the full daily budget.

This release includes several improvements that make budgeting and stepped-device control more stable.

2.5.1.en: Fixed an issue where a stepped load device would be prioritised behind a binary device.

2.6.0.en: Support stepped load for zaptec devices (still requires a flow). Support boost mode for EV chargers. Support passing in battery as state-of-charge to chargers.

2.6.2.en: Improve EV charger UX by consolidating amp tags.

2.6.3.en: Set step matching-card now supports value in Amps.

2.7.0.en:
You can now set deadlines for your devices. Tell PELS when your EV should be charged or when a room should be warm by, and it will plan the cheapest hours to get there while respecting   your power and budget limits. A new Smart tasks tab shows what is planned and what has already run, and each device on the overview gets a pill you can tap to set or change its deadline. EV support is on by default, and PELS now learns how much power each device actually draws so its plans get more accurate the longer you use it.

The overview and daily budget views surface a lot more of what PELS is actually doing and why. The hero tells you at a glance whether you are on track for the day, how today is shaping up compared to your budget, and the reason behind each decision PELS is making. If the budget you have set can’t fit the day ahead, you are warned up front and pointed at the Adjust tab, where you can drag a range, preview the result side by side, see exactly what would change, and undo if you don’t like it. Device status is written in plain language now: instead of internal terms, devices say things like Limited, Resuming, Charging paused, Lowered by PELS or Waiting for available power, and Smart tasks show why a plan has no allocation yet when that happens.

Prices and plans are also more dependable: cached prices survive app restarts and the change of day, smart task plans are saved so they come back exactly as they were, transient hiccup when talking to Homey are retried automatically, and available-power readings stay accurate when a single device reading is briefly missing.

2.7.1.en: Fixed a theming issue. Homey dark mode applies a blanket hue rotation on top of everything, includign the PELS iframe. This should now make the colours render correctly at least for light mode and for mobile.

2.7.2.en: Fixed a performance issue and several other stability and UX issues.

2.8.0.en: Add trigger card and global tokan containing calculated prices per hour.

2.9.0.en: Add the option to allow smart tasks to exempt from budget and to limit other devices. Also add option to switch phase mode for EV chargers.

2.10.0.en: Adds widgets for available power and smart tasks. Also adds a mode selector to the PELS insights app.

2.11.0.en: New dashboard widgets to create a smart task (with plan + cost preview) and rescue held-back devices. Smart tasks now switch their device off cleanly when finished, and rescued devices get priority to claim power. Native stepped control is on by default for Høiax heaters, with a warning when a Flow conflicts with PELS. Refreshed settings design throughout.

2.11.1.en: Improved the smart task planner. Also includes various UI tweaks.

2.11.2.en: Tweaks for widgets and improved trajectory estimates.

2.11.3.en: Fixed a bug in the smart task planner. Also includes various UI tweaks.

2.11.4.en: Device pages now show an Activity log of recent actions PELS took. Plan widget layout improvements. Various stability fixes.

2.11.5.en: Added workaround for Homey sometimes failing to load widgets. Various other stability and UI tweaks.

2.12.0.en: PELS can now set tomorrow's budget based on learnt daily consumption and weather forecast.

2.13.0.en: Devices held back by today's budget now offer a quick option on the Overview to let them run anyway until they reach their normal target, matching the rescue already available from the dashboard widget. The Budget tab's chart now traces a steady budget pace line and lets you switch between viewing energy used and estimated cost.

2.13.1.en: Managed devices now ease off gradually toward the end of each hour instead of all at once, plus more reliable handling of power readings that come in through a Flow.

2.13.2.en: Fixed a few calculation issues for homes with solar.

2.14.0.en:
PELS can now put excess solar power to use at home instead of exporting it. On heating devices where you turn on the new 'Use solar surplus' option, which appears once you have a solar inverter, PELS raises the target slightly while you have surplus solar so the energy is used at home, and the Overview explains when this is happening.

Home batteries and solar inverters are now recognised and accounted for, without PELS trying to control them, and they no longer clutter the device selection lists. Price levels are also handled correctly during periods when electricity prices go negative, alongside smaller fixes to battery status display and to how device readings are refreshed.

2.14.1.en:
Managed heating devices that pause within their own temperature range are no longer mistaken for not responding, so you will see fewer false warnings on a water heater or thermostat that is simply holding its temperature. When a device does stop drawing power well below its target, the on-screen note is now calmer and points to a concrete thing to check.

This release also includes a behind-the-scenes fix that keeps electricity price updates working reliably after the price service changed its security certificate, plus minor internal improvements.

2.15.0.en:
PELS now shows what your solar is doing: today's production, how much you used at home, how much was exported, and the money you saved or earned. You will find it on the Usage tab and on each solar device. Homes without an export meter can put surplus to use too. PELS works out the excess your panels are holding back and gently runs eligible heating and simple on/off devices to soak it up at home instead of losing it. You can also set your export price so savings and planning reflect what you actually earn.

The settings screens have had a big refresh: clearer, more legible text, calmer charts that use one colour per meaning, and a single consistent navigation and back pattern throughout. Smart tasks can now optionally pause lower-priority devices to help an important task reach its goal in time.

Behind the scenes, PELS now plans against the price it actually acts on, which is your import price adjusted for the solar you have available. This release also adds stability fixes: more reliable electricity price updates when the price feed returns unexpected values, a fix for high processor use in homes where background usage sat above the limit with nothing left to pause, and several corrections to solar accounting.

2.16.0.en:
You can now change a smart task's finish time or target, or clear it entirely, straight from the task's own page. The Overview has been made clearer and more consistent: every device now describes its state in the same plain wording, a new line under the summary points out a smart task that is behind or at risk, and the budget view leads with the estimated cost for the day. The warning for going over your hard cap now reflects where this hour's energy use is heading rather than a single momentary spike, so it is steadier and more accurate.

This release also fixes several issues. In homes where background usage sat above the limit with nothing left to pause, the app could work the processor hard enough to restart; a boosted water heater or similar device could take several minutes to reach full power; and a charger controlled through a flow could get stuck when resuming from off. Projected energy for the hour no longer shows a negative figure while you are exporting solar.

2.17.0.en: When you use Homey Energy as your power source, you can now choose which device PELS reads as your whole-home power meter instead of relying only on Homey's automatic pick. This helps in homes where the automatic choice isn't the meter you want PELS to measure. Also includes a few other minor UX tweaks.

2.17.1.en: Fix missing devices in power meter dropdown.

2.17.2.en: Fixed an issue where an inactive or unplugged EV charger could prevent devices such as water heaters from resuming even when enough power was available.

2.17.3.en: Fixed so that a device that change step during off state is reconciled when turned back on.

2.17.4.en: Fixed some parts of the overview page where PELS was not entirely honest about what was limting the home.

2.17.5.en: Fixed a case where an EV charger could stay paused for several minutes into a new hour despite ample available power.

2.17.6.en: An EV charger that reports plugged-in but idle (i.e not just paused) can now be started, and smart tasks will plan for it. This means PELS will also authenticate an Easee charger itself.

2.18.0.en:
New setting for devices PELS can switch on and off: Leave off until turned on again. When it is enabled and you turn the device off yourself, in Homey or from another automation, PELS leaves it off and uses the freed power elsewhere instead of resuming it. Turning the device back on hands it straight back to normal control, and a smart task that needs the device will show it is at risk while it stays off.

Also fixed an issue where a paused EV charger could keep every other limited device from resuming, leaving them off even when there was power to spare.

2.19.0.en:
Added beta support for meter areas. PELS can now manage separate parts of a property, such as an apartment, garage, or cabin, using their own power meter and capacity limit. Devices are assigned from their Homey zones, and each area can have its own operating mode and simulation setting.

The Overview and Usage pages can now be switched between meter areas, and capacity warnings identify the affected area. This update also includes fixes for area-specific device control meter selection, and resuming heating devices.

2.19.1.en:
This test release adds independent operating modes for each meter area, including per-home mode selection, device priorities, and temperature targets.

It also improves how PELS responds when devices are turned off elsewhere, initializes stepped loads more safely, and explains how Safe pace now is calculated more clearly.

2.19.2.en: Remove some churn around stepped devices, especially when using smart tasks. Overview should be more clear when a device is turned off externally.

2.20.0.en:
Smart tasks are easier to adjust: you can change a task's extra permissions directly from the task editor, and tasks now keep their permissions when you edit them. There is also a new option to disable temperature control for individual thermostats, so PELS only switches them on or off and never changes their setpoint. A new Flow trigger fires when power stays above the hard cap for a number of seconds you choose; the existing alert card now reacts immediately, including on brief spikes.

Smart tasks now reserve the power they need to start instead of turning off devices that are already idle. The daily budget behaves more steadily after mid-day changes, the suggested budget now responds when your current budget has been limiting devices, and status texts explain more accurately why a device is idle or waiting to resume.

2.20.1.en: Fixes thermostats being limited to on and off switching even when temperature control was left enabled for them.

2.20.2.en: Devices waiting for power now say how much more power is needed before they can resume, updated every cycle, and the amount reacts to the current situation rather than a fixed figure. The Overview no longer blames the car when it was PELS that paused the charger, the managed and background split is shown when managed usage is a known zero, and device cards now describe what that device needs while the hero line states what is limiting the home. Smart tasks and other budget-exempt work can resume while the daily budget is holding other devices back, as long as there is capacity for them, and ties between equally cheap hours now pick the earliest hour.

2.21.0.en:
You can now tell PELS which cars charge at a given charger. Open the charger's page, tick the cars that use it, and PELS matches one when it plugs in and reads its battery level, so charge boost and smart tasks know how full the car is without setting up a Flow. The charger card shows that battery level, and when a car is associated it can say for itself whether it is the one holding up charging, including when the car and the charger disagree about what is happening.

The 'Waiting for car' line no longer appears on a charger that is simply switched off, and a smart task created while tomorrow's prices are already available no longer claims it is waiting for prices.

2.21.1.en:
A device that is waiting for power now tells you how long it has been held and how much more power it needs, instead of naming the limit that applies to the whole home. The badge and the widget chip use one wording for every kind of hold, holds longer than an hour are shown in hours rather than as a large number of minutes, and the 'Let it run now' action is offered for any device that is being held back rather than only some of them. A device waiting because this hour's energy budget is used up now says exactly that, instead of promising more budget next hour, which was not always true.

Diagnostics reports are more useful: repeated solar and battery readings no longer fill up the log with the same value, and the device information PELS is asked to include is now complete and no longer cut short.

2.22.0.en:
Smart tasks now follow your device priorities: when two tasks compete for the same cheap hours, the task on the higher-priority device is planned first, and every device now has its own place in the priority list instead of sharing a rank with others. Homes that report power through a Flow can now use the solar features: report a negative number when you export, and PELS picks up your solar production, shows the solar summary on the Usage tab, and can run selected appliances on solar surplus.

EV charging is more careful: PELS learns which charging powers your charger actually accepts and stays within them, and when a paused charger does not start again it waits and explains why instead of repeating the command. An associated car's battery level now survives a replug and is shown without a misleading staleness note. When the home is above the hard cap, PELS now turns down the device the meter shows is drawing, even if that device's own power reading lags behind, and a device that is held back so another can start now names the device it is waiting for.

2.23.0.en:
Every device's page is now built around what that device is. It opens with what the device is doing right now, its current draw, and why it is held, an EV charger gets a Charging card for charge boost and a Car card showing the associated car's battery, thermostats show their temperature per mode, and the activity log lists newest events first with repeats collapsed. A new Power when running field in Setup shows the figure PELS plans with for that device, says where the figure came from, and lets you correct it or leave it empty for automatic — previously this was only possible through a Flow. PELS also remembers the highest power it has measured for each device, so its estimates survive a restart instead of starting over.

Smart tasks book the day's hours more accurately: hours late in the day are no longer skipped when earlier hours went over plan, an hour with limited room is used for the minutes it affords instead of being passed over entirely, and a task that could not book an hour no longer switches its device off during it — the device keeps running normally when there is power for it. A stepped device set up without any usable power step is no longer paused in a way it could never resume from, and a device that goes offline stops counting its last power reading in the Usage tab.

2.23.1.en:
A device set up with power steps is now recognised as a stepped device consistently, so it shows its steps and its current level instead of appearing as a simple on and off device. When several devices are waiting for power to free up, only the one that is genuinely next shows the countdown, and the others say they are behind it. A stepped device waiting for more power now says it is waiting to increase rather than waiting to resume, and a thermostat resting near its target no longer shows a hold reason, since the card already shows the current and target temperature. Stepped devices now also wait for the whole-home power reading to settle after any device resumes, so a step increase is no longer decided on a stale reading.

Smart tasks explain a missed target more accurately: a run that was short on power or time is no longer reported as having needed more energy than estimated. The automatic daily budget now judges a day by the energy it actually held back at the end of the day rather than by how long devices waited, so a day where everything still ran does not push the budget up. An electric car that goes offline no longer keeps reporting its last known battery level, and the link to its charger is restored automatically when the car returns.

2.23.2.en:
Right after a device resumes, a brief power spike no longer makes PELS switch off other devices straight away: while the resumed device is still settling and the hour has room, PELS waits a short moment bounded by the energy at stake before limiting anything, so thermostats and water heaters are no longer paused for spikes that resolve on their own. Devices that are switched on or off are now confirmed on the device's own acknowledgement rather than on what it does afterwards, so a slow-starting EV charger is no longer reported as not responding and its charging starting or stopping is picked up as an ordinary reading. When several meters are marked as tracking total home consumption, PELS no longer guesses which one is the whole-home meter under Automatic; choose the correct meter directly under Power source, as the setup guide now describes.

The Overview shows one Boost state for every kind of device, explained as being given priority over other devices, and a car that is unplugged below its charge level no longer claims that priority. A thermostat is shown as a temperature card only when both its current and target readings are available, a stepped device that cannot reach the level it was asked for no longer shows as resuming, and the power bar always names whether this hour's pace or today's budget sets the safe pace. Smart task history is now kept safely when the app briefly cannot read it, and a settings change of an unexpected kind no longer stops the settings screen from updating.

2.23.3.en:
The Overview now lists every device PELS manages, each saying what it is doing right now and why it is limited or waiting. The list is there from the start: after a restart or on a new install, devices appear immediately and say they are waiting for the first power reading, instead of the page staying empty until the first plan. Device states on the page follow the device live rather than a snapshot that could be many minutes old, and a device lowered to a smaller level is shown as limited at that level rather than as turned off.

The limiting behaviour you choose for a device is now the furthest PELS may go, not what always happens: a charger set to turn off is lowered step by step first and only paused when lowering is not enough. A device you switch yourself is taken into account in the next decision instead of being put straight back the way the plan had it. When the whole-home meter goes silent, PELS no longer trusts the last reading indefinitely: after ten minutes without a reading it plans again and limits devices if needed, rather than holding a decision made before the meter went quiet. Turning off temperature control for a device now disables only the temperature adjustments, and its other controls keep working.

2.23.4.en:
A smart task on an EV charger now says the car is not plugged in, instead of reporting a problem with the car's battery reading. Previously a charger with no charging session could report an out-of-date battery level for the whole length of a task, which pointed at a fault that was not there. A device that is being switched off is no longer shown as resuming while that command is still on its way.

Turning Managed by PELS off for a device no longer makes its smart task look like the device has gone missing. The task is paused rather than deleted: it says it is paused because the device is not managed, keeps its target and ready-by time, and resumes once you turn the switch back on. If the ready-by time passes while it is still paused, the run ends the same way any other unfinished run does.

2.23.5.en:
Every thermostat PELS manages now has a temperature for each mode, including devices you never set one for on the Modes screen. Previously a heater with no target for the current mode could stay at a lowered temperature after being limited, with nothing to bring it back to. PELS now fills in a target from the device's own current setting, so there is always a value to return to, and price and solar adjustments apply to it the same way they apply to a target you set yourself.

After a restart, the Overview and the Available power widget no longer present the previous run's readings as current. Until the first power reading arrives they say that no recent reading is available instead of showing old numbers. Devices with power steps, such as EV chargers and water heaters, are no longer sent the same command over and over when they are slow to confirm it, and a device that needs to be limited is no longer skipped because another device was limited moments earlier. Learned power figures, solar forecast history and the record of devices left switched off are now kept safely when the app briefly cannot read them after starting.

2.24.0.en:
A managed device with power steps can now follow your solar instead of running as hard as your hard cap allows. On its device page, an EV charger set to an EV control mode gets a Charge on solar surplus switch, and any other device you have set up with steps gets Match solar surplus. PELS then picks the level your export covers and moves it up and down as the sun changes. Increases wait a couple of minutes so a passing cloud does not change the level every few seconds, and decreases happen straight away.

There is a floor to this. A charger cannot go below 6 A, which is about 1.4 kW on one phase and 4.1 kW on three, and when your surplus cannot cover even that PELS stops the device. Where it stops is the choice you already made under Power limiting for that device, so a charger set to be turned off stops charging, while one set to a level keeps drawing at that level from the grid. Your hard cap and daily budget still come first, and a smart task with a deadline on the device decides while it is running.
